bull_bear.body:
- Recently launched 'Turquoise' brand under which three projects have been launched and two more are in the pipeline, giving a single consumer-facing identity across the portfolio
- Land bank positioned in prime and developing locations of Ahmedabad, Gujarat — a concentrated but established micro-market
- Marketing capability supported by administrative processes and standardisation of onsite and offsite processes (Board's Report)
- Long Term Bank Facility of Rs.151 Crore rated IVR BBB-; Stable by Infomerics Valuation and Rating Limited during the year under review
- Experienced management team and customer-centric approach cited by management as the basis for capitalising on emerging opportunities (MD&A Outlook)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Revenue lumpiness from project-completion timing and revenue-recognition cycles — Management states FY 2025-26 performance was impacted primarily by the timing of revenue recognition and project execution cycles inherent in the real estate business, and that revenues were lower because of the timing of project completions. With a single reportable segment and a small number of projects, reported revenue swings sharply between years for reasons unrelated to underlying demand.
- Geographic and single-segment concentration in Ahmedabad, Gujarat real estate — The Company operates in a single reportable segment, namely Real Estate, and its projects are clusters of residential and commercial spaces located on prime and developing locations of Ahmedabad, Gujarat. Any local slowdown, land-price or approval shock in that one micro-market hits the whole portfolio at once.
- Interest-rate and inflation sensitivity affecting housing affordability and demand — MD&A Opportunities and Threats states that fluctuations in interest rates and inflation may affect housing affordability and impact consumer purchasing decisions, and that any slowdown in economic growth, reduction in disposable incomes or adverse changes in employment conditions could lead to moderation in demand across residential and commercial segments. The Outlook section repeats interest-rate fluctuation as a live challenge for FY 2026-27.
- Input-cost inflation, land acquisition costs, labour shortages and supply-chain disruption — MD&A Threats flags increasing land acquisition costs, rising prices of construction materials, labour shortages and supply chain disruptions, which may affect project timelines and profitability — the direct margin and delivery-schedule risk for a developer.
- Regulatory, approval and taxation risk — MD&A Threats flags regulatory changes, delays in obtaining statutory approvals, environmental compliance requirements and changes in taxation policies as factors that may further impact project execution and development costs. For a RERA-regulated developer, approval delay translates directly into carrying cost and delivery slippage.
- Competitive intensity from established developers and shifting customer preferences — MD&A Threats notes heightened competition from established developers, evolving customer preferences, and geopolitical uncertainties affecting investment flows, which may influence market dynamics — relevant given the Company is building a new consumer brand ('Turquoise') against incumbents.
- Liquidity and financing availability for both the developer and homebuyers — MD&A Threats states the sector remains sensitive to changes in liquidity conditions and availability of financing, which could affect both developers and homebuyers. The Board's Report records a Long Term Bank Facility of Rs.151 Crore rated IVR BBB-; Stable — a sub-investment-grade-adjacent rating that makes funding cost and access a structural watch item, and the Company also took unsecured loans from its Directors during the year.
- Risk management is a Board-reviewed framework rather than a committee-driven quantified process — MD&A Risk and Concern describes a well-defined risk management procedure covering risk identification, exposure, potential impact and mitigation, with the Board periodically reviewing risks. No risk register, no quantified exposures and no Risk Management Committee are disclosed in the routed sections, so the framework's effectiveness cannot be assessed from the report.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company acquires land and develops it into residential and commercial buildings, equipping them with amenities and facilities, principally in and around Ahmedabad, Gujarat. It operates in a single reportable segment, namely Real Estate, and has recently consolidated its launches under the 'Turquoise' brand. Development is carried out both directly and through a wholly owned subsidiary and associate LLPs engaged in the same land-acquisition-and-development activity.
business.title: What they do

business.body: - **Real Estate:** Turquoise Greenr, Turquoise Dreamz, Turquoise Grandeure, Turquoise Splendour, Turquoise Glamoure
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- Ratnabhumi Techno Engg Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary; the Company acquired 100% shareholding, the acquisition transaction completing on 25th April 2023. Engaged in the acquisition/purchase of land, developing it into residential or commercial buildings and equipping them with amenities or facilities. Reporting period 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026. Also appears as a related party in the Section 102 explanatory statement on related-party transactions, where it is described as a subsidiary. Note: Form AOC-1 Part A prints the name as 'Ratna Techno Engg Private Limited' while the Board's Report prints 'Ratnabhumi Techno Engg Private Limited'; treated as one entity.
- Raivat Projects LLP — associate: Associate LLP, incorporated 31st July 2017 and associated with the Company from 31-07-2017; the Company holds 68% of the shares/contribution. Significant influence arises from participation in policy decisions / Board rights; not consolidated as the Company has only significant influence and not control. Engaged in acquisition/purchase of land and its development into residential or commercial buildings with amenities or facilities. Also named as a related-party counterparty in the Section 102 explanatory statement.
- Rajul Projects LLP — associate: Associate LLP, incorporated 20th July 2017 and associated from 20-07-2017; the Company holds 52.50%. Not consolidated as the Company has only significant influence and not control. Engaged in acquisition/purchase of land and its development into residential or commercial buildings with amenities or facilities. Also named as a related-party counterparty in the Section 102 explanatory statement.
- Ratnamani Buildspace LLP — associate: Associate LLP, incorporated 20th April 2017; the AOC-1 Part B associate column shows an association date of 01-09-2021 and a 23.34% holding. Not consolidated as the Company has only significant influence and not control. Engaged in acquisition/purchase of land and its development into residential or commercial buildings with amenities or facilities. Also named as a related-party counterparty in the Section 102 explanatory statement, where the Managing Director is described as a Designated Partner having 23.34% contribution in the LLP.
- Ratna Anu Buildspace LLP — related party: Counterparty listed in the Section 102 explanatory statement on related-party transactions requiring shareholder approval; a Ratna group entity in which the Managing Director is a Designated Partner. Not listed among the subsidiaries or associates in Form AOC-1 or the Board's Report. The RPT table in this bundle is badly OCR-garbled and the column-to-counterparty mapping is not reliable, so the exact nature of the relationship beyond 'related party / Ratna group LLP' cannot be read off it.
- Ratna Harmony Buildspace LLP — related party: Counterparty listed in the Section 102 explanatory statement on related-party transactions requiring shareholder approval; a Ratna group entity in which the Managing Director is a Designated Partner. Not listed among the subsidiaries or associates in Form AOC-1 or the Board's Report. Name read from a heavily OCR-garbled table header; treat the exact spelling as approximate.
- Mr. Kaivan Shah — related party: Managing Director of the Company, named as a related-party counterparty in the Section 102 explanatory statement. The Board's Report separately records that the Company took unsecured loans from Directors of the Company during the year under review.

outlook.body:
- Consolidate operations and rationalize the business while exploring opportunities in the development of residential and commercial projects (Board's Report).
- Build out the recently launched 'Turquoise' brand as the single consumer-facing identity, with three projects launched (Turquoise Greenr at Shela, Turquoise Dreamz near Sindhubhavan Extension, Turquoise Grandeure at Godhavi) and two more (Turquoise Splendour, Turquoise Glamoure) moving to full-swing construction.
- Concentrate development on clusters of residential and commercial spaces in prime and developing locations of Ahmedabad, Gujarat.
- Maintain timely project execution, high quality standards and customer satisfaction, supported by prudent financial and risk management practices (MD&A Outlook for FY 2026-27; sourced from the profile bundle, where the Outlook section is complete — this bundle's copy is truncated mid-sentence).
- Sustain operational efficiency, prudent cost management and effective project execution, and strengthen operational processes despite lower revenue arising from the timing of project completions and revenue recognition (MD&A Operational Performance; sourced from the profile bundle).
- Standardise onsite and offsite processes and support them with marketing and administrative capability (Board's Report).
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Expansion is project-led rather than plant-led. The Company is developing clusters of residential and commercial spaces on prime and developing locations of Ahmedabad, Gujarat, and has consolidated its launches under the recently launched 'Turquoise' brand, with three projects launched under it: 'Turquoise Greenr' at Shela, Gujarat, 'Turquoise Dreamz' near Sindhubhavan Extension, Ahmedabad, and 'Turquoise Grandeure' at Godhavi. Two further projects under the same brand umbrella, Turquoise Splendour and Turquoise Glamoure, are stated to be in the process of moving into full-swing construction in the months to come; no commissioning dates, saleable areas or rupee outlays are given. Development capacity is also held through a wholly owned subsidiary, Ratnabhumi Techno Engg Private Limited (acquired 100%, transaction completed 25th April 2023), and three associate LLPs, all engaged in acquiring land and developing it into residential or commercial buildings. The Company states there were no changes in authorised or paid-up share capital during the year and no material changes or commitments affecting its financial position between the year end and the date of the Report; Infomerics assigned IVR BBB-; Stable to a Long Term Bank Facility of Rs.151 Crore.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The Indian real estate sector is expected to maintain its positive growth trajectory, supported by sustained urbanization, rising disposable incomes, favourable demographics and increasing demand for quality residential and commercial developments.
- Continued government emphasis on infrastructure development through PM Gati Shakti, Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT, metro rail expansion and enhanced urban connectivity is expected to create new growth opportunities for the sector.
- Stable macroeconomic fundamentals, easing inflationary pressures and a supportive policy environment are expected to improve consumer sentiment and support housing demand during FY 2026-27.
- The residential real estate market is likely to remain resilient, with continued demand across the affordable, mid-income and premium housing segments, driven by increasing home ownership aspirations and favourable demographic trends.
- Growing institutional participation, foreign direct investment and increasing adoption of REITs are expected to strengthen liquidity and enhance investor confidence in the sector.
- Increasing focus on sustainable construction practices, green buildings, energy-efficient designs and smart technologies is expected to reshape the real estate landscape and create long-term value.
- Commercial real estate is expected to benefit from continued expansion of Global Capability Centres (GCCs), technology companies, flexible workspaces and demand for high-quality office infrastructure.
- Company-specific: FY 2025-26 performance was impacted primarily by the timing of revenue recognition and project execution cycles inherent in the real estate business — a mix/phasing driver management flags explicitly.
- Management flags the offsetting drag from fluctuations in interest rates, input cost inflation, regulatory changes and geopolitical uncertainties, while maintaining that the long-term outlook remains positive on favourable structural fundamentals.
